sections.title: Situation
sections.prompt: What was the setting, what failed, and is the story's scope right for your level?
criteria: Names the company type, their role and one number for scale in three sentences or fewer
States the failure as their own decision ('I recommended', 'I chose'), not as bad luck or the team's mistake
Quantifies the damage in money or volume, with the arithmetic shown
Checks the story's scope (orgs, money, people) against the level they are interviewing for

sections.title: Stakeholders
sections.prompt: Who was affected or in conflict, what did each want, and how did you bring them along?
criteria: Names the person they were in conflict with and what that person was protecting
Shows at least three stakeholders wanting incompatible things
Includes the customers who were harmed, and what they needed
Ends with one idea that ties the stakeholders together

sections.title: Options
sections.prompt: When the failure surfaced, what could you do, and what would each option cost?
criteria: Lists at least three options, including the one the conflicting peer wanted
Prices each option over the same remaining period
Rules out at least one option on a hard limit (capacity, time or contract), not on preference
Puts the options on one table with the same criteria

sections.title: Decision and Trade-offs
sections.prompt: What did you decide, and what did you or your org give up?
criteria: Makes one clear call in the first person
Names a trade-off they paid from their own budget, roadmap or credibility
Says whether the call was reversible and what would have reversed it
Explains how the conflict was resolved, not just that it ended

sections.title: Economics
sections.prompt: What did the failure cost, what did your call save, and what would the right process have cost?
criteria: Derives the cost of the failure from volume, error rate and unit cost
Compares the cost of the options over the same period
Prices the counterfactual: what following the original plan would have cost
Labels every assumed figure as assumed

sections.title: Org and Ownership
sections.prompt: Who owned the response, and what ownership changed afterwards?
criteria: Names themselves as accountable for the failure and the response
Gives the conflicting peer a defined role in the response
Names an ownership or process change that outlasts the incident

sections.title: Plan and Milestones
sections.prompt: What happened in what order, from discovery to relaunch?
criteria: Gives the time from discovery to decision in hours or days
Shows the conflict conversation happening before the decision was announced
Has a relaunch with measurable gates, not a single switch back on
Includes a review that was shared beyond their own team

sections.title: Risk and Governance
sections.prompt: What risks remained after your call, and what rule changed so the failure can't recur the same way?
criteria: Quantifies the risk that remained after the decision
Names a control for the harmed customers, such as proactive outreach
States a governance change in specific terms, such as who can skip a launch gate
Names a kill criterion that was agreed in advance

sections.title: Metrics
sections.prompt: What was the measured result, and what guard shows the fix didn't move the harm elsewhere?
criteria: Gives a quantified result with a before and after number
Pairs it with a guard metric, such as hold time or repeat contacts
Says what happened to the program or the relationship afterwards
Labels any figure that is part of the story's assumed outcome

sections.title: Communication
sections.prompt: How do you tell the primary story in two minutes, and how does the other story use the same structure?
criteria: Tells the primary story in STAR order in about two minutes, in the first person
Retells the other story (conflict or failure) in the same STAR structure
Says what they would do differently, specifically, and what they changed as a result
Gives the people they had to tell (exec, peer, team) a different one-line message each
